# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (reporting line not stated) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public-benefit structure and safety-centered identity create a different bar for commercial architecture than a conventional AI vendor. Partner deployments must translate Claude’s capabilities into customer outcomes without
weakening expectations around reliability, security, or responsible use.

The operating tension is scale versus consistency: Anthropic needs partners to extend enterprise reach and implementation capacity, while retaining technical, product, and safety standards across a rapidly expanding ecosystem.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a frontier-AI, platform-led company with a hybrid enterprise motion: direct product adoption through Claude and APIs, amplified by cloud, technology, and services partners.

Its commercial identity is not simply model access. The company positions Claude as an assistant for complex knowledge work, including analysis, coding, and problem solving, while differentiating around safe, accurate, secure, reliable,
interpretable, and steerable AI.

The central operating challenge is converting a research-rooted safety thesis into repeatable enterprise adoption. This requires technical teams that can make partner-led implementations practical without turning Anthropic into a bespoke
services organization.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic is a San Francisco-headquartered public benefit corporation founded in 2021. Its public-benefit form reinforces that commercial growth is expected to coexist with a stated mission to build beneficial AI systems.

The business has multiple adoption surfaces: Claude as an end-user product and Claude-based developer and enterprise integrations. This creates a portfolio tension between product-led self-service experiences, strategic enterprise
deployments, and ecosystem-led distribution.

For partnerships, decision rights will matter. Partners need enough technical guidance and reusable assets to deliver independently, while Product and Engineering need clean feedback from deployments rather than fragmented one-off
requirements.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI leaders including Dario and Daniela Amodei.

The relevant stakeholder map spans:
- Partnerships and GTM leadership, which set ecosystem priorities and commercial coverage.
- Sales leadership, which needs partners to expand account access and delivery capacity.
- Product and Engineering, which must turn recurring deployment needs into scalable platform capabilities.
- Research, safety, and policy functions, which anchor the company’s responsible-AI positioning.
- Partner technical leaders, whose ability to scope, build, and support customer solutions determines ecosystem quality.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic’s platform value proposition combines Claude’s user-facing assistant experience with developer-oriented capabilities. Claude is positioned for analyzing information, writing code, and working through complex problems.

The architecture conversation is therefore likely to extend beyond model selection. It includes enterprise integration patterns, application design, production reliability, security expectations, developer workflows, and mechanisms for
evaluating whether an AI-enabled workflow is dependable enough to deploy.

Anthropic’s emphasis on interpretability and steerability raises the standard for field architecture. Technical recommendations must be credible both to builders seeking speed and to enterprise stakeholders seeking controls, predictability,
and trust.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly organizes its ecosystem around cloud, technology, and services partners. That is evidence of a deliberate multipartner adoption model rather than an exclusively direct-sales approach.

The partner motion appears designed to connect several capabilities:
- Cloud partners provide distribution, infrastructure context, and routes into enterprise accounts.
- Technology partners extend Claude into broader application and workflow ecosystems.
- Services partners supply implementation capacity, industry expertise, and customer-change support.
- Partner enablement becomes a strategic control point because deployment quality affects both adoption and Anthropic’s safety-centered brand.

The strongest ecosystem contribution is likely not partner recruitment alone. It is creating repeatable solution patterns, technical readiness, and feedback loops that allow partners to deliver Claude-based outcomes with less dependence on
Anthropic’s internal specialists.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s visible expansion of a dedicated partner network signals a maturing commercial model: ecosystem participation is being formalized across cloud, technology, and services categories.

The urgency is driven by enterprise AI adoption moving from experimentation toward implementation. In that environment, hyperscalers, technology platforms, and major service providers increasingly influence which AI products get evaluated,
integrated, governed, and scaled.

Competitive pressure is therefore operational as much as technical. Anthropic must make its platform easy for partners to position and deploy while preserving the differentiation associated with trustworthy AI.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Building repeatable partner-led technical motions rather than relying on bespoke field support.
- Enabling cloud, technology, and services partners to deliver production-grade AI solutions.
- Translating AI platform capabilities into enterprise architectures, deployment patterns, and measurable use cases.
- Establishing feedback loops from customer deployments into product, engineering, and GTM priorities.
- Balancing fast adoption with security, reliability, governance, and responsible-AI requirements.
- Leading technical teams through ambiguity, ecosystem scale, and cross-functional decision making.
- Creating partner enablement assets, reference patterns, and technical communities that reduce time to value.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s partner network spans cloud, technology, and services firms, making technical consistency across the ecosystem a meaningful operating challenge.
- Claude’s positioning around complex analysis and coding creates a practical opening to discuss production deployment, not just AI experimentation.
- The company’s safety and public-benefit orientation makes responsible scaling a distinctive commercial and technical concern.
- A partner-led model requires more than alliance coverage; it depends on partners being able to scope and deliver reliable customer outcomes.
- The role sits at the intersection of partner readiness, enterprise architecture, product feedback, and field execution.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume and proof graph.

Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.
"
}

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (reporting line not stated) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public-benefit structure and safety-centered identity create a different bar for commercial architecture than a conventional AI vendor. Partner deployments must translate Claude’s capabilities into customer outcomes without
weakening expectations around reliability, security, or responsible use.

The operating tension is scale versus consistency: Anthropic needs partners to extend enterprise reach and implementation capacity, while retaining technical, product, and safety standards across a rapidly expanding ecosystem.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a frontier-AI, platform-led company with a hybrid enterprise motion: direct product adoption through Claude and APIs, amplified by cloud, technology, and services partners.

Its commercial identity is not simply model access. The company positions Claude as an assistant for complex knowledge work, including analysis, coding, and problem solving, while differentiating around safe, accurate, secure, reliable,
interpretable, and steerable AI.

The central operating challenge is converting a research-rooted safety thesis into repeatable enterprise adoption. This requires technical teams that can make partner-led implementations practical without turning Anthropic into a bespoke
services organization.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic is a San Francisco-headquartered public benefit corporation founded in 2021. Its public-benefit form reinforces that commercial growth is expected to coexist with a stated mission to build beneficial AI systems.

The business has multiple adoption surfaces: Claude as an end-user product and Claude-based developer and enterprise integrations. This creates a portfolio tension between product-led self-service experiences, strategic enterprise
deployments, and ecosystem-led distribution.

For partnerships, decision rights will matter. Partners need enough technical guidance and reusable assets to deliver independently, while Product and Engineering need clean feedback from deployments rather than fragmented one-off
requirements.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI leaders including Dario and Daniela Amodei.

The relevant stakeholder map spans:
- Partnerships and GTM leadership, which set ecosystem priorities and commercial coverage.
- Sales leadership, which needs partners to expand account access and delivery capacity.
- Product and Engineering, which must turn recurring deployment needs into scalable platform capabilities.
- Research, safety, and policy functions, which anchor the company’s responsible-AI positioning.
- Partner technical leaders, whose ability to scope, build, and support customer solutions determines ecosystem quality.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic’s platform value proposition combines Claude’s user-facing assistant experience with developer-oriented capabilities. Claude is positioned for analyzing information, writing code, and working through complex problems.

The architecture conversation is therefore likely to extend beyond model selection. It includes enterprise integration patterns, application design, production reliability, security expectations, developer workflows, and mechanisms for
evaluating whether an AI-enabled workflow is dependable enough to deploy.

Anthropic’s emphasis on interpretability and steerability raises the standard for field architecture. Technical recommendations must be credible both to builders seeking speed and to enterprise stakeholders seeking controls, predictability,
and trust.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly organizes its ecosystem around cloud, technology, and services partners. That is evidence of a deliberate multipartner adoption model rather than an exclusively direct-sales approach.

The partner motion appears designed to connect several capabilities:
- Cloud partners provide distribution, infrastructure context, and routes into enterprise accounts.
- Technology partners extend Claude into broader application and workflow ecosystems.
- Services partners supply implementation capacity, industry expertise, and customer-change support.
- Partner enablement becomes a strategic control point because deployment quality affects both adoption and Anthropic’s safety-centered brand.

The strongest ecosystem contribution is likely not partner recruitment alone. It is creating repeatable solution patterns, technical readiness, and feedback loops that allow partners to deliver Claude-based outcomes with less dependence on
Anthropic’s internal specialists.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s visible expansion of a dedicated partner network signals a maturing commercial model: ecosystem participation is being formalized across cloud, technology, and services categories.

The urgency is driven by enterprise AI adoption moving from experimentation toward implementation. In that environment, hyperscalers, technology platforms, and major service providers increasingly influence which AI products get evaluated,
integrated, governed, and scaled.

Competitive pressure is therefore operational as much as technical. Anthropic must make its platform easy for partners to position and deploy while preserving the differentiation associated with trustworthy AI.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Building repeatable partner-led technical motions rather than relying on bespoke field support.
- Enabling cloud, technology, and services partners to deliver production-grade AI solutions.
- Translating AI platform capabilities into enterprise architectures, deployment patterns, and measurable use cases.
- Establishing feedback loops from customer deployments into product, engineering, and GTM priorities.
- Balancing fast adoption with security, reliability, governance, and responsible-AI requirements.
- Leading technical teams through ambiguity, ecosystem scale, and cross-functional decision making.
- Creating partner enablement assets, reference patterns, and technical communities that reduce time to value.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s partner network spans cloud, technology, and services firms, making technical consistency across the ecosystem a meaningful operating challenge.
- Claude’s positioning around complex analysis and coding creates a practical opening to discuss production deployment, not just AI experimentation.
- The company’s safety and public-benefit orientation makes responsible scaling a distinctive commercial and technical concern.
- A partner-led model requires more than alliance coverage; it depends on partners being able to scope and deliver reliable customer outcomes.
- The role sits at the intersection of partner readiness, enterprise architecture, product feedback, and field execution.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume and proof graph.
